why: PL-PSLICE 10-18: HBM SU programme per-quarter cluster pslice_c5 (pgp_<q>) as a LANDED parent. Its S leaves (TT boundary insertion 309.5 / FF 252.6) and L leaves (483.1 / 394.7) are 174 ps apart, and the cluster is 1.73 x 0.95 mm: one balanced tree cannot hold <= 80 ps at both corners (c_b16 lesson), so the leaves sit in their own clock regions and every head <-> leaf / port -> leaf net is landed.

regions.name: h
regions.why: head (configuration pin stage + column decode + fault OR) alone in the central channel: every leaf region is then landed from it alike (no alignment pads)

regions.name: l
regions.why: the three L leaves (13 dictionary banks, boundary insertion TT 483 / FF 395), bottom-left row

regions.name: sw
regions.why: three S leaves (TT 310 / FF 253), top-left row (MX)

regions.name: se
regions.why: four S leaves on the E side (bottom c0 c4 R0, top c8 c9 MX); column 0 drives busy / valid / done / edge_index

lag_pins.why: status return: the head configures every leaf (cfg landed +3 into each leaf region) and ORs their sticky faults / checks their valid lockstep; that is a cross-region loop, so the status inputs are landed back and read at one common lag (all leaves alike: no false lockstep fault)

bench.why: load phase (cycles < 8000: a configuration write on half the edges, every row / local bank) then run phase (starts 1 in 40, rare writes 1 in 100 so the write-on-start leaf fault rises late and is compared through the lagged status path)

mut_waivers.4: PL-PSLICE bench 10-18 (ot-epyc5): MUT 4 (u_c0 reset run one stage long) PASSES lockstep over 20,000 edges because every child of this parent is reset-phase-insensitive: no free-running state (the producer is idle until a start; SRAM is not reset), so one more reset edge is invisible unless a write lands on exactly that edge. The reset offsets themselves are proven by MUT 0 (every child reset delayed t(child) + RB) and the flat-eq bench.
